shortDescription: China's coal imports fell 2% in August from a year earlier to 42.09 million metric tons, customs data showed on Tuesday, as domestic supply constraints eased.

children: China's coal imports fell 2% in August from a year earlier to 42.09 million metric tons, customs data showed on Tuesday, as domestic supply constraints eased.
August's total was also down from 43.73 million metric tons in July.

"A modest month-on-month decline in import volumes suggests China's domestic coal supply constraints somewhat eased in August," said Toby Hassall, lead coal analyst for LSEG. Vessel tracking data indicated imports from Australia and Indonesia were lower in August, Hassall said.
A gas explosion at Shanxi's Liushenyu coal mine on May 22 that killed 82 people forced a squeeze in domestic supply as many mines halted production to conduct safety checks.
In the first seven months of the year, imports rose 3% to 310.19 million tons, the data showed.

Fossil-fuelled power generation, which comes mostly from coal, fell 3.5% in July as rainfall in the southwest boosted hydropower, the first year-on-year decline this year. August figures will be released later this month.
